text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Croatia may join the system of European traffic corridors by the end of June after approval by the Paneuropean Conference of Transport Ministers in Helsinki, transport ministry official Dragutin Subat said.
- Dubrovnik is likely to see 70 percent more tourists this year which still makes only 28 percent of pre-war results in peak 1990.
- President Tudjman will win with over 60 percent vote in the first round of presidential elections according to recent polls ordered by his ruling party campaign team.
- "Nothing in Croatia must depend solely on one man," liberal opposition candidate Vlado Gotovac told the audience in his campaign speach on Zagreb's main square.
- Fresh syndicated loans to Zagrebacka and Rijecka Banka reflect Croatia's good credit rating, says Zagrebacka's chief executive Franjo Lukovic.
- Teachers will name their school principals, instead of being appointed by the Education Ministry according to a new draft law on education.

- Tourism minister Niko Bulic and general director of Croatia Airlines Ivan Misetic sign a subsidy contract, reducing plane fare for Dubrovnik this summer. Beneficiaries will pay 30 percent less but must spend at least a week in the area.

- "Ruling HDZ party creates an atmosphere of lynch convincing people that we (opposition) would ruin Croatia", says social-democratic presidential candidate Zdravko Tomac. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
